This matter is taken up through Hybrid arrangement (video conferencing/physical mode).
This writ petition has been filed by petitioner Anjali Behera seeking direction on the opposite parties to provide a job to her sons as per the direction of this Court vide order dated 21.06.2023 passed in W.P.(C) No. 15298 of 2023 dated & the R&R Policy, 2006 and quash the order dated 16.08.2024 passed by the opposite party no.2 under Annexure-17.

Ms. Deepali Mahapatra, learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that while deciding Misc. Case No. 13 of 2023 as per order dated 26.04.2023 passed by the Collector and District Magistrate,
Angul, opposite party no.2 on the representation of the petitioner to provide employment and compensation towards land, houses and trees etc., came to hold that the petitioner had constructed two room asbestos houses over the disputed land only after publication of the notification under section 11(1) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (hereafter the '2013 Act') and such type of construction is not within the ambit of the said Act entailing compensation for such construction.

1 of availability of different tree growth along with tube well and asbestos rooms over the said 90 Sq.ft. which are the developments made after section 11(1) notification is also not believable.

The opposite party no.2 also observed that regarding less compensation, it is clear that the computation of compensation has been made in accordance with First Schedule of the 2013 Act observing all relevant provisions of the said Act and thus, such claim merits no consideration.

It is further observed that with regard to job benefit, in absence of cogent evidence on record so as to prove that the said asbestos house was constructed before section 11(1) notification and the petitioner was residing preceding three years i.e. the cut-off date for consideration of job benefit, such claim is also untenable and accordingly, the claim of the petitioner was found to be devoid of merit.

The petitioner challenged the said order before this Court in W.P.(C) No. 15298 of 2023 and the Division Bench of this Court vide order dated 21.06.2024 has been pleased to quash the said order dated 21.06.2023 passed by the opposite party no.2 in Misc. Case No. 13 of 2023 and directed the opposite parties to take necessary steps for disbursement of the compensation amount as well as R.R.
benefits in favour of the petitioner in accordance with law.

Ms. Mohapatra, learned counsel for the petitioner further contended that after receipt of the order,
the Special Land Acquisition Officer, NTPC in a non- speaking order has been pleased to hold that the land compensation amount to the tune of Rs.35,46,091/- has been disbursed to the petitioner and as per the R.R. Policy of 2006, the petitioner is not coming within the category of displaced family and hence, she is not eligible to get any R.R. benefits.
Learned counsel for the petitioner drew the attention of this Court to the various grounds taken in the writ petition and submitted that the petitioner is entitled to get the R.R. benefits and therefore,
the impugned order under Annexure-17 is not justified.
Issue notice to the opposite parties on the question of admission indicating therein that the matter shall be disposed of at the stage of admission.
Learned counsel for the State accepts notice on behalf of opposite parties nos.1 to 3.
Three extra copies of the writ petition along with enclosures be served on learned counsel for the State by Wednesday (08.01.2025).
Requisites for issuance of notice on opposite party no.4 by speed post with proof of delivery be filed by that date.
List this matter in the week commencing from 10th February 2025.
Counter affidavit, if any, be filed in the meantime after serving a copy of the same on the learned counsel for the respective parties.
